info.title: Replyze API
info.summary: Conversations, messages, contacts, knowledge base and analytics of a Replyze workspace.
info.description:
The Replyze REST API reads and changes one workspace: its conversations and messages, contacts, knowledge base and analytics. It is part of the Pro and Business plans (and the free trial).

**Authentication.** Make an API key in Settings → Developer (owners and admins) with the scopes it needs, and send it as `Authorization: Bearer rpz_live_...`. A key acts as the workspace, not as a person; it is shown once, stored hashed, and can be revoked at any time. A write scope includes the read scope of the same resource.

**Requests and answers.** JSON in, JSON out. Single objects are returned as they are, each with an `object` field naming its type. Times are ISO 8601 in UTC.

**Pagination.** Lists answer `{ "object": "list", "data": [...], "has_more": true, "next_cursor": "..." }`. Pass `cursor=<next_cursor>` for the next page and `limit` (1 to 100) for its size. Most lists are newest first; a conversation's messages are oldest first. `updated_since` (ISO 8601) returns only what changed since then, for syncing.

**Errors.** `{ "error": { "code": "insufficient_scope", "message": "...", "details": { ... } } }` with the HTTP status: 400 bad request, 401 `missing_api_key` / `invalid_api_key` / `api_key_revoked` / `api_key_expired`, 403 `insufficient_scope` / `plan_required`, 404 `not_found` (also for another workspace's records), 409 `contact_exists` / `idempotency_in_progress`, 422 `validation_failed` (with `details.errors` per field) / `idempotency_key_reused`, 429 `rate_limited`, 500 `server_error`.

**Idempotency.** Send `Idempotency-Key: <a unique value>` with a POST. Sent again with the same key in the next 24 hours, it returns the first answer (with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`) instead of doing it twice, so a retry never sends a message twice.

**Rate limits.** 120 requests a minute per key. Every answer has `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix time); a 429 has `Retry-After` (seconds).

**Audit.** What a key changes, and every conversation or contact it reads, is in the workspace's audit log (Settings → Audit log) under the key's name.

**Webhooks.** Replyze can also call you: see the webhooks section for the events, their payloads and how to verify the signature. Zapier, Make and n8n connect today with their HTTP modules: a webhook trigger (Catch Hook) for events, and HTTP requests with the API key for actions.

get.description: The key the request is made with, its effective scopes and its workspace. Use it to test a connection.

The teammates who can answer conversations (owners, admins and agents, not viewers), for `agent_id`.

Scope: `conversations:read`.

Conversations as the inbox lists them (with something the visitor or the team wrote; not spam unless `status=spam`), newest first.

Scope: `conversations:read`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only this status. `spam` lists the spam inbox.

parameters.name: contact_id
parameters.description: Only this contact's conversations.

parameters.name: assigned_agent_id
parameters.description: Only those assigned to this teammate.

parameters.name: unassigned
parameters.description: Only those assigned to nobody.

parameters.name: team_id
parameters.description: Only those assigned to this team.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Only this channel.

parameters.name: tag_id
parameters.description: Only those with this tag.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Matches the contact's name, email or phone, the subject, and what was said (not internal notes).

parameters.name: created_since
parameters.description: Only conversations started since then.

post.description:
Starts a conversation with a contact, opened by a message.

- `from: "agent"` (the default): a message from the team, sent to the contact on the channel (the web chat when `channel_id` is left out; on email, WhatsApp, Telegram, Messenger or Instagram the contact must be reachable there).
- `from: "contact"`: a message from the contact (a form submission, a call note): it lands in the inbox like any visitor message, notifies the team and runs the automations. The AI does not reply to it.

The contact is `contact_id`, or found by `contact.email` (then `contact.phone`) and made when there is none.

Scope: `conversations:write`.

contact.description: Found by email (else phone) or made.

channel_id.description: One of the workspace's channels. Default: the web chat.

subject.description: The subject (the email subject on email).

agent_id.description: Assign it to this teammate; a message from the team is from them.

example.subject: Your order #1042
example.message: Hi Jane, your order has shipped!

x-codeSamples.label: curl
x-codeSamples.source:
curl -X POST 'https://client.replyze.chat/api/v1/conversations' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REPLYZE_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"contact":{"email":"jane@example.com","name":"Jane Doe"},"subject":"Your order #1042","message":"Hi Jane, your order has shipped!"}'

get.description:
One conversation of the workspace (404 for any other). Logged in the audit log.

Scope: `conversations:read`.

post.description:
Give it to a teammate (`agent_id`) and/or a team (`team_id`; the team's routing picks a teammate when it assigns automatically). `null` takes it off them. At least one of the two.

Scope: `conversations:write`.

Marks it resolved. When the workspace has them switched on, the visitor gets the closing message and the rating request, as when the team resolves it in the inbox.

Scope: `conversations:write`.

Opens a resolved conversation again.

Scope: `conversations:write`.

Adds a tag: an existing one by `tag_id`, or by `name` (made when the workspace has no tag with it).

Scope: `conversations:write`.

delete.description:
Takes the tag off the conversation (the tag itself stays).

Scope: `conversations:write`.

get.description:
The conversation's messages, oldest first (50 a page by default): the visitor's, the team's, the AI's and the team's internal notes (`is_internal_note`).

Scope: `conversations:read`.

parameters.name: include_notes
parameters.description: false leaves internal notes out.

post.summary: Send a reply or a note
post.description:
`type: "reply"` (the default) goes to the visitor on the conversation's channel (widget, email, WhatsApp, Telegram, Messenger, Instagram) exactly as a reply from the inbox: the team sees it live, a resolved conversation opens again. `type: "note"` is an internal note: the team sees it, the visitor never does.

With `agent_id` the message is from that teammate (and a reply assigns them an unassigned conversation); without it, from the team.

Scope: `conversations:write`.

example.content: Thanks for waiting! Your refund is on its way.

x-codeSamples.label: curl
x-codeSamples.source:
curl -X POST 'https://client.replyze.chat/api/v1/conversations/123/messages' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REPLYZE_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"content":"Thanks for waiting! Your refund is on its way."}'

One message of the conversation.

post.description:
A new contact. An email another contact has is refused with 409 `contact_exists` (its id in `details.contact_id`): update that one instead.

Scope: `contacts:write`.

get.description:
One contact. Logged in the audit log.

Scope: `contacts:read`.

patch.description:
Changes the fields sent. `custom_data` is merged: keys not sent stay, a key sent as null is removed. `tags` replaces the list.

Scope: `contacts:write`.

get.description:
Knowledge base articles, newest first, without their content (get one for it).

Scope: `knowledge:read`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only this status.

parameters.name: category_id
parameters.description: Only this category.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: Only this language (en, de, pt-BR...).

parameters.name: q

post.description:
A new article, a draft unless `status` is published. Its slug comes from the title unless given; published, it is on the public help center (when that is on) and the AI answers from it.

Scope: `knowledge:write`.

x-codeSamples.label: curl
x-codeSamples.source:
curl -X POST 'https://client.replyze.chat/api/v1/articles' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REPLYZE_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"title":"How long does shipping take?","content":"Orders ship within 24 hours.\n\nDelivery takes 2 to 4 business days.","status":"published"}'

get.description:
One article with its content (Markdown or HTML, as written).

Scope: `knowledge:read`.

patch.description:
Changes the fields sent. Every change is kept in the article's history in the editor.

Scope: `knowledge:write`.

x-codeSamples.source:

What the AI would answer a question from: published articles first, then the best passages of the website pages and files it learned, each with where it is from.

The Analytics page's headline numbers for the last `days` days and the same span before them: conversations, resolved, handled by the AI alone, response times, satisfaction, and the split by channel. Pro and Business (not the trial).

A conversation's first message from the visitor or the team: from then on the inbox lists it.

Sent as a JSON POST to the webhook's URL, signed: see the X-Replyze-Signature header.

parameters.name: X-Replyze-Event
parameters.description: The event name.

parameters.name: X-Replyze-Event-Id
parameters.description: A copy of the body's `id`. **Not signed**: a replayed request can carry any value, so drop duplicates by the `id` in the verified body.

parameters.name: X-Replyze-Timestamp
parameters.description: A copy of the body's `created_at`, in Unix seconds. **Not signed**: a replayed request can carry any value, so check the age of the `created_at` in the verified body.

parameters.name: X-Replyze-Signature
parameters.description: `sha256=` and the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with the webhook's signing secret (shown once when the webhook is added). Only the body is signed, not the other headers.

id.description: The event's id: the same on every retry. Drop an event whose id you have already handled.

created_at.description: When the event happened. Refuse an event more than 5 minutes from now: it is an old request sent again. Five minutes leaves room for the retries.

2XX.description: Received. Any 2xx counts; a network error or a 5xx is retried twice (after 30 seconds, then 3 minutes) with the same body; any other answer is final.

tools.title: Search conversations
tools.description: Find conversations in the inbox, newest activity first. Matches the contact's name, email or phone, the subject, and anything the visitor or the team wrote (not internal notes). Filter by status, contact or assignee. Returns up to `limit` conversations with their contact, assignee, channel and tags; use get_conversation to read one.

tools.name: get_conversation
tools.title: Read a conversation
tools.description: One conversation with its latest messages, oldest first: what the visitor wrote (sender_type "visitor"), the team's replies ("agent"), the AI's replies ("bot") and the team's internal notes (is_internal_note true, never shown to the visitor).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.title: List teammates
tools.description: The teammates who can answer conversations, with their ids (for assign_conversation and agent_id), roles and whether they are online.

tools.name: send_message
tools.title: Reply to the visitor
tools.description: Send a reply in a conversation. The visitor gets it, in the chat widget or by email, WhatsApp, Telegram, Messenger or Instagram, whichever channel the conversation is on. A resolved conversation opens again. Write it as the team would: it is sent as is. For something only the team should see, use add_note.

tools.name: add_note
tools.title: Add an internal note
tools.description: Add an internal note to a conversation: the team sees it in the inbox, the visitor never does. Use it for summaries, findings and handover notes.

tools.name: assign_conversation
tools.title: Assign a conversation
tools.description: Give a conversation to a teammate (agent_id from list_agents) and/or a team (team_id). Send null to take it off them. At least one of agent_id and team_id is needed.

tools.name: search_contacts
tools.title: Search contacts
tools.description: Find contacts (the workspace's customers and visitors who gave their details) by name, email, phone or company. Newest first.

tools.name: get_contact
tools.title: Read a contact
tools.description: One contact with their details, custom data and latest conversations.

tools.name: search_knowledge
tools.title: Search the knowledge base
tools.description: Search what the workspace's AI answers from: published knowledge base articles, and the website pages and files it learned. Ask in plain words, like a customer would. Each result says where it is from (article, website page with its URL, or file).

tools.title: Read an article
tools.description: One knowledge base article with its full text, by id or by slug. Drafts included (status says which).

signature_examples.source:
import hashlib, hmac, json, time
from datetime import datetime

def verify(raw_body: bytes, headers, secret: str):
    """The event, or None when the signature doesn't match or the event is more than 5 minutes old."""
    expected = ('sha256=' + hmac.new(secret.encode(), raw_body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()).encode()
    given = headers.get('X-Replyze-Signature') or ''
    # Compare bytes: compare_digest raises TypeError on a str with non-ASCII characters.
    if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, given.encode('utf-8', 'replace')):
        return None

    # Signed, so take the time and the id from the body: X-Replyze-Timestamp and
    # X-Replyze-Event-Id are unsigned copies that a replayed request can change.
    event = json.loads(raw_body)
    sent = datetime.fromisoformat(event['created_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00')).timestamp()
    if abs(time.time() - sent) > 300:
        return None
    return event  # then skip it if you have already handled event['id']
